premises.text: Valuable status reports and similar business communications stay trapped in email, so companies make worse decisions, duplicate work, and lose money
premises.evidence_span: these communications that are loaded with valuable business information are sent by email from one person to another, and the rest of the company can't access them

premises.text: ThinkFuse lets managers set who reports, when, and what template in ~30 seconds, then reminds writers so reports are consistent, timely, and shared
premises.evidence_span: all we need to know is who you want status reports from, when you want them, and what information they should include

premises.text: Shared recipient lists and follow-a-project (Twitter-like) make status reports designed-to-be-shared rather than private email
premises.evidence_span: each of these people can follow a project just as easily as they can follow someone on Twitter

premises.text: Across-company status reports form a business graph of people-project relationships searchable for expertise and client relationships
premises.evidence_span: Using status reports, we're mapping the relationships between people and projects in a company

premises.text: Access, consistency, and power of shared status reports align people and resources across the organization
premises.evidence_span: making status reports more accessible, by making them more consistent, and more powerful to align people and resources

value.text: Everyone understands the whole puzzle—better-informed decisions and aligned work from accessible status reports
value.evidence_span: each person understanding the entire puzzle and where their pieces fit in

causal_links.evidence_span: decisions are less informed, work is duplicated, and ultimately, companies lose money

notes: Manager setup + writer UX + follow + search examples folded as cascade of shared-status product and business-graph mechanism (§4.1.7). Alignment claim kept as outcome condition of the same product. No separate monetization module. Transcript cuts mid-sentence. Singleton D1: email-trap problem independently revisable.
